film.master: Hero V7.mp4 (94MB, h264, yuv420p, bt709) — not in the repo, see .gitignore

relationshipToV6.verdict: Same shoot, re-cut longer. Not new footage.
relationshipToV6.evidence: All seven beats present in the same order with the same shots, including the graphic surgical close-up that V6 already had. 42.167s vs 35.285s (+19.5%), 1011 vs 846 source frames.
relationshipToV6.consequence: Every line of copy carried over unchanged. The work was re-extract, re-time, re-point — not re-write.

frameBudget.why: Holds V6's exact temporal density (14.18 fps vs 14.17) so the scrub feels identical. Client chose this over 550 and 500 when shown the payload cost.

measuredEncode.note: V7 is 16% heavier in total but 7% LIGHTER per frame than V6. The early estimate of 105MB came from a 14-frame sample that over-weighted the two extreme close-ups (315KB and 497KB); the full run came in below it.

beats.shot: Reception. Three arches, TPL roundel lit on the centre arch, two desk iMacs, two staff in black, a client arriving in cream.
Consultation. Wide white void; female client seated, male clinician standing in a white coat with a clipboard.
Diagnostics. Practitioner in black presents a scored analysis dashboard on a tablet to a seated male client; blood-tube rack on a stand behind.
beats.behaviour: Film keeps advancing; text fades in, holds, fades out. No freeze, no links.
beats.why: Client's decision on V6, kept: unnumbered, comes and goes without stopping the film. Carries no links, because a link that fades while the film scrubs cannot be clicked reliably.

beats.shot: Hair, extreme close-up. Gloved hands placing an applicator and syringe into the scalp; practitioner's head left, client's head centre.
beats.why: The wide hair shots leave only ONE cell clearing AA. All 121 frames of the shot were swept in sliding 14-frame windows; 431-444 bottom-right was the lowest-variance window that clears (261-290 variance vs 1343 in the wides). It is also the stronger shot.

beats.shot: Body. Client lying on a treatment table, practitioner applying a handheld device, console at frame right.
beats.why: Cell analysis said top-centre (luma 234, variance 1.4, 12.79:1). In the browser that measured 1.22:1, because the block is 432px tall in a 242px cell and its lower half sat over the practitioner. Right column measured 11.90 and was taken instead. The top-down body shot (out 357) was tested and rejected: best cell there is 4.84:1.

beats.shot: Theatre, wide. Three staff in blue scrubs around a client on a table under a surgical light.
Dispensary. Product shelf, brand boards — SkinCeuticals, Korean Skincare, La Roche-Posay, CeraVe, Hair Care Products.

timeline.note: The 460vh figure that used to sit in index.html was V5's and had been stale through all of V6.

method.globalMotion: mean abs luma diff between adjacent source frames, 480x270 greyscale, smoothed +/-2
method.plateaus: runs of >=6 source frames under the 25th percentile of smoothed motion
method.copySpaceFirstPass: 3x3 grid at full resolution; per-cell mean luma, variance, 5th percentile, per-cell motion
method.copySpaceCorrected: THE CELL IS THE WRONG REGION. Blocks overflow their cells (432px block, 242px cell), so cell statistics miss what is below. Final ink figures are the 5th-percentile contrast of the BLOCK'S OWN FOOTPRINT sampled off the painted canvas via getImageData, which is also the only measurement that accounts for the cover-crop (the canvas shows the middle 1728 of 1920 at 1440x900).
method.contrast: WCAG relative luminance, dark ink #242424, worst case = darkest end of the background distribution

encodeFidelity.note: V6 shipped a gamma bug once: ffmpeg's PNG muxer stamps cICP/cHRM/gAMA and decoders applied a shift worth 7.2/255. V7 writes PNG via Pillow, which emits no colour chunks, so the bug cannot occur. Drift here is under 0.27/255 — rounding noise, not a shift.

notes: No scrim. Every beat clears WCAG AA for #242424 with ZERO darkening; the worst is hair at 10.69:1 (5th pct) / 9.01:1 (1st pct).

Resolution ceiling unchanged from V6: the master is 1920x1080 and the stage rasterises larger on a DPR-2 display, so the engine caps its backing store rather than upscaling. A 4K master is still the only real fix.
Face has no footage in any master supplied. It is a nav pillar and a card in the phone deck, not a film beat.
